summary: Aermotor steel lookout on Shoestring Butte, Lake County, OR, built 1931 with a cabin; sold for scrap in 1968, and no source describes the site today.

facts.design: Aermotor steel tower with a 7x7 cab
facts.status_note: Sold for scrap in 1968; the towers had not been removed as of October 1968. Two listings say gone by 1968
facts.agency: U.S. Forest Service, Fremont National Forest

events.note: Aermotor steel tower and 12x16 living quarters erected; the 73-foot height is from the 1959 inspection and firelookout.com, the register says 100 feet
Cox Creek fire, early August 1931, could not be located from any lookout point; the new tower covered the area
Major improvements to the living quarters: new cabinets, linoleum, sealing and a new roof
Regional inspection found the premises clean and orderly; guy wire, landing boards and stair fencing needed work
Forest Supervisor memo of October 26, 1961: tower has no living quarters; if funds for the replacement cannot be made available, requests funds for a trailer house as living quarters
Screens checked and safety devices fitted to the trap door, completed June 1962
Two steel towers, including Shoestring, offered to the Army in the fall of 1967 (letter of May 13, 1968 says 'last fall'); the Army did not take them
Towers sold for scrap in October 1968 but not yet removed; two listings say gone by 1968

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Register says 100 feet; firelookout.com and the 1959 inspection quoted on the Forest Lookouts page say 73 feet; a 1931 entry says a 75-foot tower was nearing completion. Kept 22.3 m (73 feet) because two sources and a dated inspection agree on it.

notes_for_editor: Height conflict is the main open point (100 ft register vs 73 ft inspection vs 75 ft in a 1931 note). Note the firelookout.com index row for Shoestring Butte, Lake County, lists coordinates 42.59306, -121.26905, which do not match the record (42.38634, -120.53286 per firetower.org). The record coordinates were kept: the 1948 survey description quoted on the Forest Lookouts page places the summit about 17 miles northwest of Lakeview, which fits. The index row should be checked. The Forest Lookouts page also covers Slide Mountain in the same 1967-68 scrap story; keep Slide Mountain details out of this record. No source describes the summit or the site today, and access is unknown.
